key_insight: ProtoDiffusion generates editable, multi-layer images using one shared spatial prototype and one vector per layer, reducing latent token count from NHW to HW+N before backbone-specific packing.
engineering_relevance: This compact representation supports image- and text-conditioned design generation without requiring layer counts or layouts as inputs, while allowing optional bounding-box guidance.
method: ProtoVAE encodes designs into a shared spatial prototype and per-layer candidate vectors.
A shared decoder reconstructs each RGBA layer conditioned on its candidate vector.
Latent diffusion jointly denoises the prototype and fixed candidate slots, leaving unused slots empty.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 40.43 dB layer-crop reconstruction PSNR, LayerD image-to-design RGB L1 of 0.040 with boxes, and text-to-design FID of 66.41 versus 86.84 for FLUX.2 [klein], with 19.1× faster generation than a same-backbone generation-then-decomposition cascade.
watch_item: The fixed candidate-slot set imposes a layer-capacity ceiling, and the reported token reduction alone does not establish memory or runtime savings across backbones.
paper_title: ProtoDiffusion: Token-per-Layer Generative Modeling of Multi-Layer Images
